title: Using the Ehrenfest theorem for determining the self-focusing and self-trapping of nonlinear beams
authors: Chandroth P. Jisha, Stefan Nolte, Alessandro Alberucci
abstract: We discuss how to generalize the Ehrenfest theorem for the computation of the width of nonlinear waves obeying the nonlinear Schrodinger equation. To do that, we model the nonlinear potential as a quantum harmonic oscillator (QHO) whose strength depends on the power and on the wavefunction width. We apply the model to different types of nonlinear responses, eventually comparing the results with numerical simulations. Our model has the advantage of explaining the main properties of nonlinear confined waves, such as stability and breathing, in a relatively simple and intuitive manner.
summary: This paper develops an advanced theoretical method by generalizing the Ehrenfest theorem to analyze nonlinear wave propagation. It models the nonlinearity using a Quantum Harmonic Oscillator potential, leading to solvable ordinary differential equations for the beam width. This framework successfully predicts key phenomena such as self-focusing and stable light localization (breathers) in various optical media.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining the self-focusing and self-trapping behavior of nonlinear optical beams.
main_result: The authors develop a generalized framework using an ODE derived from the Ehrenfest theorem to model beam width evolution, showing it can explain stability and breathing in various nonlinear regimes.
method: The method involves generalizing the Ehrenfest theorem by modeling the nonlinear potential as a Quantum Harmonic Oscillator (QHO) whose strength depends on power and beam width. This leads to solving high-order ordinary differential equations for the beam width squared ($w^2$).
model_or_system: The system is nonlinear wave propagation governed by the Generalized Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation (GNLSE), applied to optical beams in media exhibiting various nonlinear responses (local, nonlocal). The analysis focuses on the evolution of the beam width $w(z)$ along the propagation direction $z$.
key_observables: Beam width ($w$), self-focusing/self-trapping behavior, and the existence of stable solutions like breathers.
important_parameters: Nonlinearity strength parameters ($\gamma, N, M$), input power relative to critical power ($P/P_{cr}$), and nonlocal length scales ($l$).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include assuming radial symmetry, approximating the nonlinear potential as parabolic (QHO model), and making approximations like neglecting derivatives of optical power with respect to $z$ (adiabatic drop).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the GNLSE and generalizing the Ehrenfest theorem, deriving a fourth-order ODE for beam width ($w^2$), simplifying this into various second-order ODEs based on approximations (e.g., adiabatic drop), and finally analyzing specific cases like Kerr or nonlocal nonlinearities.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum mechanical theorems (Ehrenfest) with classical wave phenomena (nonlinear optics), providing a powerful, simplified analytical tool to predict complex beam dynamics like self-focusing without full numerical simulation.
